name: Hisquierdo v. Hisquierdo
summary: The Supreme Court held that the Railroad Retirement Act preempted California community property law from treating railroad retirement benefits as divisible marital property, setting out the test for federal preemption in the domestic relations context.
significance: This case established the framework for analyzing when federal benefit statutes preempt state domestic relations law in the division of marital property, making it foundational for disputes over federally regulated retirement assets in divorce.
